questions.question: What is distance?
choices: The total length of a traveled path
The shortest directed change in position

questions.question: What is displacement?
choices: The force required to move an object
The total path length regardless of direction
The directed change from initial to final position

questions.question: What information distinguishes velocity from speed?
What is acceleration?
choices: Change in velocity per unit time

questions.question: Which unit is commonly used for speed?
How is average speed calculated?
choices: Total distance divided by elapsed time
Elapsed time divided by total distance

questions.question: On a position-versus-time graph, what does slope represent?
Why can an object accelerate while keeping constant speed?
choices: Acceleration depends only on increasing mass
Constant speed requires a changing temperature
Its direction of motion can change

questions.question: What does a horizontal line on a position-versus-time graph mean?
choices: The object moves faster each second
The object moves in a circle

questions.question: How does a steeper positive slope on a position-versus-time graph compare with a shallower positive slope?
choices: It indicates a longer elapsed time only
It indicates a greater positive velocity

questions.question: Why must a reference point be specified when describing motion?
choices: Position and motion are described relative to a reference frame
Every object has the same velocity for all observers
Reference points determine an object's mass
Motion requires a moving observer in every case

questions.question: An object slows while moving east. In which direction is its acceleration?
How can average speed differ from the speed at a particular instant?
choices: Average speed always equals the highest speed reached
Instantaneous speed measures mass rather than motion
Motion can vary during the measured interval

questions.question: What does a straight line with negative slope on a position-versus-time graph indicate?
choices: Speed increasing toward the positive direction
Constant velocity in the negative direction
